body:
sophie: FYI ACME Prod reported a sharp drop in embeddings throughput around 03:00 UTC. Tokens/sec steady but vectors/sec ~6x down. Saw a flurry of 401s during a token rotation, then lots of retries and big batch submissions.
jason: Any dimension mismatch errors or mostly auth/retry noise?
sophie: Quick logs excerpt pasted below. Not seeing dimension errors in the first pass.
```
2026-03-16T02:58:12Z INFO request id=abc123 user=acme-prod model=redwood-embed-1 batch_size=64 vectors=64 dim=512
2026-03-16T03:00:58Z WARN auth token=acme-prod status=401 msg="invalid token"
2026-03-16T03:01:05Z WARN gpu-queue depth=912 host=gpu-7 svc=embed-srv p95_latency_ms=1420
2026-03-16T03:01:06Z INFO request id=abc400 user=acme-prod batch_size=256 vectors=256
2026-03-16T03:01:10Z ERROR response id=abc999 status=500 msg="kvcache OOM allocate 8MB"
2026-03-16T03:02:00Z INFO retry storm count=120 api_key=acme-prod
```
maya: Two hypotheses: (A) token rotation caused clients to retry with default large batch size -> queue surge, or (B) routing changed to a slower quantized variant under load.
jason: I grepped logs for "dimension mismatch" in that window: count=0. But I do see many batch_size=256 requests from acme-prod at 03:01.
arjun: Reminder: under heavy contention we route to vq-128 variant which can be 2-3x slower when KV cache churn is high. Concurrent big batches + fallback routing = queue backup.
ops-bot: ALERT channel=embed-svc customer=acme-prod p95_latency=1.42s queue_depth=912
sophie: Repro attempt: curl to embeddings with batch_size=256 using ACME key to mimic behavior.
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACME_KEY>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":["doc1","doc2",...],"batch_size":256}'
```
jason: I ran a micro-repro: batch_size=32 ~160ms, batch_size=256 ~1.3s and GPU queue spikes. That correlates.
maya: Prom queries we ran: embedding_vectors/sec by api_key and embed_queue_depth showed spike at 03:01 for acme-prod. Also saw increase in route_to_variant{variant="vq-128",api_key="acme-prod"}.
arjun: Confirmed: high fallback routing for that key during the spike.
sophie: Immediate mitigations proposed:
1) Soft cap batch_vectors for acme-prod to 64 via rate-limit rule
2) Temporarily disable fallback to vq-128 for that key (force fast path)
3) Billing to review duplicate/retry charges for credit
4) Add detection/alert for pattern: 401 spike -> batch growth -> queue spike
Can ops apply (1) and eng-runtime do (2)?
maya: Applying a per-key soft cap now (max_batch_vectors=64), rolling in 2m. Monitoring.
arjun: I'll temporarily pin routing for acme-prod to float32 fast path and add a metric for per-key variant switches.
billing: Noted the billing spike at 03:01. I'll open a provisional credit with bizops and link the support ticket. Need confirmation of duplicate retries.
sophie: After throughput normalizes, follow-ups: update SDK docs on retry/backoff defaults, recommend safe batch caps, and add an autosplitter guard to prevent single-client batch surges.
jason: I'll add a change to autosplitter: throttle single-api-key batching so one key can't fill a GPU queue.
ops-bot: RESOLVED ALERT queue_depth=120 p95_latency=180ms (after policy applied)
acme-support: Thanks everyone, throughput looks normal on our end. We'll audit our client retry logic and report back. :thumbsup:
